items.title: this is f*cking gold. a four-stroke engine has one job - suck, squeeze, bang, blow. fuel in, fire, piston down, exhaust
items.summary:
this is f*cking gold. a four-stroke engine has one job - suck, squeeze, bang, blow. fuel in, fire, piston down, exhaust out. break the loop and it’s just parts twitching.

four models, same prompt, same engine:
Claude Opus 5.5 · GPT-6 Astra · Gemini 4 Argon · Grok 4.7

three of them run the whole cycle - valves timing, combustion firing, crank turning, oil sitting in the pan. one just gestures at it, half the parts missing.

I didn’t touch a thing and I’m not scoring them. you’ve got eyes: which one’s a real working engine, and which one’s a sketch that forgot how engines work?

Opus, Astra, Gemini or Grok?

items.summary: “AI is transforming the way we engage with news and media, particularly in relation to access, reliability and trust,” Naomi Goulder, deputy dean and associate dean of Innovation and Enterprise innovation and enterprise at Northeastern University London, said in an interview with Northeastern Global News. Journalists have emphasized the value of humans gathering and confirming the accuracy of information as opposed to the AI collection of often unconfirmed commentary available on the internet. [...] At the same time, AI has had a revolutionary impact on multiple aspects of human life. In the past five years, chatbots like Claude and ChatGPT have transformed how people access information. items.title: Does AI Extend or Diminish Us? | News | shorelinemedia.net
items.summary:
Flierl explained that AI is already embedded in everyday life, from electricity and water systems to navigation and financial services. While AI can help improve hurricane forecasting, support cancer research and assist with complicated mathematical problems, Flierl cautioned that excessive reliance on it can weaken critical thinking, reduce long-term learning and diminish people’s sense of meaning and ownership in their work. [...] Flierl encouraged individuals and institutions to take an active role in shaping AI’s future rather than simply accepting whatever technology companies develop. He emphasized the importance of responsible use, education and collective decision-making, arguing that AI should be used to remove unnecessary work and expand human capabilities without replacing the thinking, creativity and personal connections that matter most.

On a slide from his presentation, Flierl quoted. [...] “It’s not the AI that’s the problem… it’s the wrong use of AI.” — Michael Gerlich, as quoted in The Chronicle of Higher Education, “The Student Brain on AI”

Flierl had conducted his own research into his slides. The presentation includes several studies, surveys and company-reported discoveries;

After the presentation there was an open Q&A session with audience members asking questions.

items.summary:
Markey is asking Alphabet if Google will commit to allowing schools to turn off AI features and chatbots in K-12 student accounts while still allowing students to access Google Search. He also requested that Google disclose any research it has conducted on the impact of its AI tools on students' mental health.

Markey has requested that Google disclose any research or testing it has conducted on the safety of its AI functions and their impact on the mental health of K-12 students. [...] Google maintains that its policy change gives schools more control over how they allow AI into schools. An Alphabet spokesperson also told CBS News that Google's AI features are now so tightly integrated into search that it cannot offer the latter without also enabling the AI services. [...] Google faces mounting public pressure to change a new policy that would limit U.S. students' access to the internet giant's widely used search platform unless schools also offer its artificial intelligence-based education tools.

In a letter to Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai on Monday, Sen. Edward Markey demanded that Google's corporate parent reverse the policy, which blocks search for K-12 student accounts that don't also provide access to apps such as Google Classroom.

items.title: Andrej Karpathy:
items.summary:
Andrej Karpathy:

“A 1B model can be much more effective than most current LLMs.

90% of current models waste a ton of capacity and money on remembering stuff that doesn’t matter.”

here is his 5 core thesis about Small LLM’s:

1. the intelligence was never the knowledge. Strip the memorized internet, keep the reasoning. What’s left is the cognitive core, and it’s small.

2. the core might fit in ~1B params. Maybe less. “Plenty of room at the bottom.” We’ve been paying for a library when we needed a brain.

3. size stopped being the bottleneck. What makes an agent work is the tools it can call and how tight the feedback loop is, not parameter count.

4. intelligence lives in the system, not the weights. A raw LLM is a CPU with no OS. Small core + good harness > giant model alone.

5. you can own it. A model on your hardware is one no one can rate-limit, price-hike, or deprecate on you.

in 12 months the gap between teams shipping on-device and teams paying per-token frontier bills won’t be capability.

TwIL an 8.8B model at 90%+ of frontier isn’t a benchmark flex.

It’s the thesis Karpathy’s been repeating all year, made real.

study more on this below ↓

Learning to reason with LLMs \| OpenAI

September 12, 2024

[Release](https://openai.com/research/index/release/)

# Learning to reason with LLMs

We are introducing OpenAI o1, a new large language model trained with reinforcement learning to perform complex reasoning. o1 thinks before it answers—it can produce a long internal chain of thought before responding to the user.

[Contributions](https://openai.com/openai-o1-contributions/) [Try ChatGPT(opens in a new window)](https://chatgpt.com/?openaicom-did=ace47a51-46de-4d9c-a6a5-e7819b768e45&openaicom_referred=true)

## This post introduced OpenAI o1.

The ChatGPT access information reflects the September 2024 launch. o1‑preview and o1‑mini have been retired from the API; o1 is deprecated. See the [API deprecation schedule⁠(opens in a new window)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations).

For the current experience:

[View current API models(opens in a new window)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models)

[Try ChatGPT(opens in a new window)](https://chatgpt.com/?openaicom-did=ace47a51-46de-4d9c-a6a5-e7819b768e45&openaicom_referred=true)

Listen to article8:58

OpenAI o1 ranks in the 89th percentile on competitive programming questions (Codeforces), places among the top 500 students in the US in a qualifier for the USA Math Olympiad (AIME), and exceeds human PhD-level accuracy on a benchmark of physics, biology, and chemistry problems (GPQA). While the work needed to make this new model as easy to use as current models is still ongoing, we are releasing an early version of this model, OpenAI o1‑preview, for immediate use in ChatGPT and to [trusted API users⁠(opens in a new window)](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/rate-limits/usage-tiers).

Our large-scale reinforcement learning algorithm teaches the model how to think productively using its chain of thought in a highly data-efficient training process. We have found that the performance of o1 consistently improves with more reinforcement learning (train-time compute) and with more time spent thinking (test-time compute). The constraints on scaling this approach differ substantially from those of LLM pretraining, and we are continuing to investigate them.

results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

args.text:
Dưới đây là hàm Python tính số Fibonacci bằng phương pháp đệ quy (recursion):

```python
def fibonacci(n):
    # Trường hợp cơ sở
    if n <= 0:
        return 0
    elif n == 1:
        return 1
    # Bước đệ quy
    return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)

# Ví dụ sử dụng:
n = 10
print(f"Số Fibonacci thứ {n} là: {fibonacci(n)}")
```

### Giải thích:
- **Trường hợp cơ sở (Base case):** Khi `n <= 0` hàm trả về `0`, khi `n == 1` hàm trả về `1`.
- **Bước đệ quy (Recursive step):** Với `n > 1`, hàm sẽ tự gọi lại chính nó để tính tổng của hai số Fibonacci trước đó: `fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)`.

[...] Earlier this year, he and his team began experimenting with a change to the way the robot code is organized. Using a framework they called Graph-as-Policy, robot tasks are segmented into individual skills, such as finding an object, planning a grasp and moving the gripper without collisions. Goldberg likened it to individual building blocks that fit together into something much larger. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.
